name: Sign/symbol interchange
statement: \text{Rewrite first: swap each pair of signs everywhere, then evaluate by BODMAS.}
derivation: Rewrite the whole expression with the new signs, one sign at a time from left to right.
Evaluate the rewritten expression by BODMAS ([[f:math-operations.bodmas]]).
Match the value with the options.
shortcut: Do the $\times$ and $\div$ parts first and the unit digits of the result often decide the option.
common_traps: Swapping only one pair and forgetting the other.
Rewriting correctly but evaluating left to right instead of BODMAS.
Evaluating the original expression first and then trying to swap signs in the answer.

name: BODMAS evaluation
derivation: Scan left to right and do every $\div$ and $\times$ in the order met: they have equal rank.
Scan again left to right and do every $+$ and $-$ in the order met: they also have equal rank.
The single number left is the value.
common_traps: Going strictly left to right: $(5+4)\times9=81$, then $(81-80)\div10=0.1$.
Doing all $\times$ before $\div$: $12\div4\times4$ becomes $12\div16$ instead of 12.

name: Swap trial to balance equation
statement: \text{For each option: apply the swap, evaluate LHS by BODMAS, keep the option with LHS = RHS.}
derivation: Evaluate the LHS as given; the gap from the RHS shows what must change.
Rank options: a swap that moves a large number into a $\times$ or out of a $\div$ changes the value most.
Apply one option's swap to the whole expression and evaluate by BODMAS.
Stop at the option that gives LHS = RHS; a quick check of one other option guards against slips.

steps: As given: $18-23\times455\div7+28 = 18-1495+28$, far below 377: a $\times$ must move to the front.

common_traps: Swapping the signs only at one place when the sign appears twice.
Swapping digits of a number instead of whole numbers (13 to 31) when numbers are to be swapped.
Evaluating each trial left to right instead of BODMAS, which can make a wrong option look right.
